subject.title: feat(linux): native gateway transport for Quick Chat — device identity, TLS pinning, ack-driven sends

question: Should a Linux Quick Chat process authenticated with local shared credentials be allowed to silently create an operator-scoped paired device identity on a direct-local Gateway connection?
rationale: The implementation deliberately extends the native-app silent-pairing trust class to a new platform and requests broad operator scopes; source and tests can verify mechanics, but cannot choose the intended product trust boundary.

options.title: Approve Linux native trust class
options.body: Keep direct-local silent pairing for `openclaw-linux` after the bootstrap and routing defects are repaired, accepting parity with the existing native-app model.

options.title: Require explicit pairing on Linux
options.body: Keep the native transport but require dashboard approval for Linux device enrollment until Linux-specific trust assumptions are formally adopted.

recommendation.title: Approve Linux native trust class
recommendation.body: Keep direct-local silent pairing for `openclaw-linux` after the bootstrap and routing defects are repaired, accepting parity with the existing native-app model.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available ownership evidence is the merged Linux Quick Chat implementation and this follow-on native transport design.
